# Results — Study 829 (Global Sovereign-Bond Momentum)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Moskowitz,
Ooi & Pedersen (2012), *"Time Series Momentum"*, applied to global government bonds: a bond
market's own **12-minus-1-month total-return trend** predicts its next month, so going long the
positive-trend and short the negative-trend markets (or long-only trend timing) should earn a
positive costed net Sharpe. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number. As-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped; **as-of 2026-06-30**). Fingerprint `fee295eff13f` (month-end price panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), resampled to **month-end**, **5 global sovereign-bond ETFs**, 2007-01-31 → 2026-06-30, **234** months (221 after the 12-1 burn-in) |
| Universe | `BWX`, `IGOV` (ex-US developed sovereigns), `BNDX` (USD-hedged global ex-US), `EMB` (EM USD sovereigns), `IEF` (7-10y US Treasury anchor) — cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each market's **12-minus-1-month total return** `mom_t = level_{t-1}/level_{t-12} − 1` (twelve-month trend ending one month ago, the standard 12-1 skip), known at the close of month `t−1` |
| Position | **long-short**: `+1` on positive trend, `−1` on negative; **long-only**: `+1` on positive trend, `0` otherwise; equal-weight across the active markets |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold month `t`. The costed backtest charges one-way `cost_bps × turnover` per rebalance and `75 bps/yr` borrow on the short-weighted NAV |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag) *t* on the monthly strategy return; one-sample *t*; a 3,000-draw block-rotation placebo; a three-era robustness cut; a lookback sweep; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** These five are *currently listed, surviving* funds;
global-sovereign / EM-debt ETFs that were wound up or merged are absent, so any positive trend
result is a **mild upper bound**. The panel is tiny by construction — only a handful of liquid
global-govvie ETFs have a decade-plus of history — which independently **limits statistical
power**; both caveats travel with the numbers.

## Benchmark — naive equal-weight buy-and-hold

Owning all five ETFs equal-weight, no timing at all:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| mean | **+24.56 bps/mo** (+2.95 %/yr) |
| Sharpe | 0.399 |
| Newey-West(6) *t* | +1.88 |

This is the honest yardstick: any "trend edge" has to beat *just holding the bonds*.

## The headline — long-short time-series momentum (`+1 / −1`)

n = **221** months:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **mean strategy return** | **+0.26 bps/mo** (+0.03 %/yr) |
| annualised vol | 5.99 % |
| Sharpe | **0.005** |
| **Newey-West(6) *t*** | **+0.02** |
| one-sample *t* | +0.02 |
| hit rate | 0.548 |

The long-short book is **flat** — the trailing 12-1 trend carries essentially **no** predictive
sign. NW *t* = +0.02.

## The headline — long-only trend timing (`+1 / 0`)

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **mean strategy return** | **+12.27 bps/mo** (+1.47 %/yr) |
| annualised vol | 4.56 % |
| Sharpe | 0.323 |
| **Newey-West(6) *t*** | **+1.75** |
| one-sample *t* | +1.39 |

The long-only variant *looks* positive — but it earns **less than half** the naive
buy-and-hold's +24.56 bps/mo (it sits out during down-trends and misses the recoveries), and its
NW *t* = +1.75 does **not** clear the |*t*| ≥ 2 bar. The apparent drift is **bond beta**, not a
trend edge.

## Placebo — is there any trend information at all?

Keep the point-in-time positions but **circularly rotate the return matrix in time** (breaks the
trend → forward-return link, preserves each market's own autocorrelation), 3,000 draws:

| variant | observed | null mean (sd) | right-tail *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| long-short | +0.26 bps | +7.46 bps (12.47) | 0.724 |
| long-only | +12.27 bps | **+13.57 bps** (6.92) | 0.533 |

Both observed values sit **squarely inside** the block-rotation null — for long-only the observed
+12.27 bps is actually **below** the null mean +13.57 bps. The trend timing adds **nothing** the
return series' own drift does not already give you; the positive long-only number is a
rotation-invariant artefact of holding bonds, not a signal.

## Robustness — three eras

| era | long-short | | long-only | |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| | mean | NW *t* | mean | NW *t* |
| 2007-2014 (n=71) | +4.65 bps | +0.23 | +26.94 bps | +1.66 |
| 2014-2020 (n=72) | −9.80 bps | −0.91 | +8.66 bps | +0.88 |
| 2020-2026 (n=78) | +5.55 bps | +0.25 | +2.25 bps | +0.29 |

No era clears the bar; the long-only "edge" fades monotonically as the great 2007-2020 bond bull
recedes (2020-2026: +2.25 bps, *t* = +0.29). And the **lookback sweep** (long-only NW *t*: 6m
+1.56, 9m +1.23, 12m +1.75, 15m +1.52) never reaches 2 at any window — the result is fragile in
the formation parameter, not robust.

## The costed backtest — can you get paid for it?

One-way `cost_bps × turnover` per rebalance; short book pays 75 bps/yr borrow.

| variant | one-way | gross/mo | cost/mo | net/mo | net Sharpe | *t* (net) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| long-short | 5 bps | +0.26 | 3.44 | **−3.18 bps** | −0.064 | −0.27 |
| long-short | 10 bps | +0.26 | 4.74 | **−4.48 bps** | −0.090 | −0.39 |
| long-only | 5 bps | +12.27 | 0.68 | +11.59 bps | +0.306 | +1.31 |
| long-only | 10 bps | +12.27 | 1.35 | +10.92 bps | +0.288 | +1.24 |

The long-short book's flat gross goes **negative** after any cost. The long-only book's costed net
Sharpe (~0.29) is just **diluted, costed bond beta** that under-earns buy-and-hold — not tradable
alpha (net *t* = +1.24, below the bar).

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded monthly panel with a persistent AR(1) trend state that (with `edge > 0`)
drives the forward month. No network.

| world | mean NW *t* | fires (\|t\| ≥ 2) |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | **−0.22** | **0/20** |
| planted (`edge = 0.010`), **20 seeds** | **+13.38** (mean Sharpe 2.45) | **20/20** |

The detector recovers a *planted* time-series-momentum effect cleanly and never fires on the
random-walk null — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine absence of edge, not a broken engine.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The claimed global-sovereign-bond time-series-momentum edge does **not**
  appear on this tape. The specified **long-short** 12-1 book is **flat** (+0.26 bps/mo, NW *t* =
  **+0.02**; block-rotation *p* = 0.72). The **long-only** variant's +12.27 bps/mo is **bond
  beta, not trend**: it under-earns naive buy-and-hold (24.56 bps/mo), its placebo observation
  sits *below* the rotation null (*p* = 0.53), its NW *t* = +1.75 misses the |*t*| ≥ 2 bar, it
  fades era-by-era, and it is fragile across lookbacks (*t* ∈ [1.2, 1.8]). A clean 20-seed
  synthetic control confirms the engine fires on a planted trend — so the null is real.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The long-short book loses money once costed (net −3.18 bps/mo at 5 bps,
  −4.48 at 10 bps; net Sharpe < 0). The long-only book's costed net Sharpe (~0.29) is diluted bond
  beta that under-earns buy-and-hold — no costed net edge survives.
